### Radial chart
Progress toward a goal drawn as rings from a data table, as concentric rings or a half-circle gauge.

Component ID: `radial-chart`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/radial-chart.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/radial-chart.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.12.0)

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: Four plan targets as a share of their goals, or seats filled out of 25 as a gauge, are a radial chart. Revenue split across plans is a pie chart.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-07); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-07, `llm.md#radial-chart`): Rings drawn clockwise from the top from a figure's data table as a share of data-max, with tracks, a legend of each row's cell for more than one row, gauge and sparkline modifiers, a <tfoot> total in the middle, further columns in the tooltip, and a pointer and keyboard tooltip that highlights the ring.

Web adaptation: The <table> stays in the page as the text alternative and the no-JavaScript fallback; the rings, total and legend are aria-hidden and the plot is one Tab stop with a polite live tooltip.

Known boundary: Drawing, the hidden table, ring geometry and colors, tracks, the legend, the <tfoot> total, the gauge's half circles, values past the maximum and missing values, thinning crowded rings, RTL, the tooltip, pointer distance hit testing, keyboard movement and destroy are checked in a browser; screen reader output, forced colors and enlarged text remain unverified. Zero and negative values leave only the track; there are no labels on the rings.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#radial-chart).

#### Contract

A `<figure class="radial-chart">` takes the same `<figcaption>` and `<table>` as a column chart. `AutoInit()` draws each row of the first value column as a ring, outermost first, filled clockwise from the top as a share of `data-max` (100 by default), with a legend of the rows and their cells when there is more than one, and a tooltip that follows the pointer across the rings. The table stays in the page, visually hidden, as the chart's text alternative; without JavaScript it shows instead of the chart.

#### Syntax

```html
<figure class="radial-chart gauge" data-max="25">
  <figcaption>Team capacity</figcaption>
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>Seats</th><th>Count</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th>Filled</th><td>18</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Offered</th><td>21</td></tr>
    </tbody>
    <tfoot>
      <tr><th>Total seats</th><td>25</td></tr>
    </tfoot>
  </table>
</figure>
```

#### Also documented

The Radial chart section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `radial-chart-is-a-figure-with-a-table`: Write .radial-chart as a <figure> holding a <table> of the data. The drawn chart is hidden from assistive technology, so the table is all a screen reader reads, and it is what shows without JavaScript.
- `radial-chart-has-a-caption`: Name a .radial-chart with a <figcaption>. It names the focusable plot as well as the figure; hide it with .visually-hidden when nearby text already names the chart.
